quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and use saddlebags. High loads on a sissy bar can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies even braking for both the front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Learns and remembers the approximate braking force used by the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies partial front braking whenever the rear brake is used. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. In poor conditions, increase this to three seconds or more.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping, even for gentle, normal stops.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage car drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle-car crashes are caused by drivers not yielding the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to riders.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up suddenly, or you may need space to escape from a vehicle coming up behind you.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Not use any brakes, but downshift.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. If you must brake, use both brakes.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are made to keep the rider cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are made to keep the rider cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Riding jackets help prevent dehydration and provide protection even in warm weather. Many jackets are designed to let air flow and keep riders cool.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. This is part of basic motorcycle safety.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Prevent access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots and surface hazards, and gives you an escape route if needed. It should not block your escape routes.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right part of your lane so they see you in their mirror.
Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see better and be more visible. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what following distance should you maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the space so drivers can see it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park a motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with the rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the same part of your lane the whole way through the curve.
Stay in the left part of your lane the whole way through the curve.
Stay in the right part of your lane the whole way through the curve.
Know that the best path may not match the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not match the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to change your lane position anytime. The best way through a curve may not follow the road's curve.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the turn's angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and use the brakes if needed.

questions.question: Lane sharing is:

options.text: Allowed in heavy traffic to use space better.
Allowed if there is enough space for both vehicles.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane width to ride safely. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes. Both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter. The brake works when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes. Both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes work together. Read your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.
